text: It's easy to assume there's one Sentinel API. There isn't. You'll reach for two separate surfaces depending on what you're asking for, and this lesson covers both: running real KQL from Python, and updating incidents directly through the same control plane the Sentinel portal itself calls.

The Log Analytics data query API runs KQL against raw workspace tables -- security incident, security alert, sign-in logs -- the same query language you already wrote by hand in the portal's Logs blade. The Sentinel management REST API, under management dot azure dot com, works with incident objects directly: list them, read one, update its status, severity, or owner. Pick KQL to analyze log data, and the incidents API to act on a specific incident as an object.

Both surfaces authenticate the same way, with an Azure AD app registration exchanged for a token through azure dash identity. A client secret credential object feeds the logs query client, which sends your KQL -- here, pulling every high or medium severity incident opened in the last twenty four hours -- and hands back rows you can convert straight into a list of dictionaries.

Closing an incident means calling the management plane instead, since the logs query client is read only. You request a token scoped to management dot azure dot com slash default, using that same credential object, then patch the incident resource with a JSON body setting status to closed and classification to true positive. One Azure AD app, two resource scopes, two completely different kinds of calls.

That split maps directly onto role assignments. Sentinel Reader is enough to run KQL queries and list incidents read only. Sentinel Contributor is required before a patch call updating status, classification, or owner will succeed. Grant the write role only to the service principal that genuinely needs to close or reassign incidents -- everything else in your pipeline should run on Reader.

You now have both halves of scripting against Sentinel: KQL for analyzing raw log data, and the incidents REST API for acting on a specific case. Next lesson moves to AWS, where Security Hub and GuardDuty expose their own finding formats through boto3 -- a different shape, but the same underlying pattern of authenticate, query, paginate.
